name: Security {OS}
tagline: Threat modelling, hardening and the security gate on a release.

commands.name: /security
commands.does: Open the authority and establish the written scope

commands.name: /threat-model
commands.does: Assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries, abuse cases

commands.name: /security-review
commands.does: Static review of auth, permissions, secrets, input handling, crypto

commands.name: /pentest
commands.does: Attempt the planned attack classes inside the written scope

commands.name: /ai-attack
commands.does: Prompt injection, tool misuse, exfiltration, tenancy leakage

commands.name: /supply-chain
commands.does: SBOM, dependency origins, pinning, advisories, build provenance

commands.name: /privacy
commands.does: Map personal data flows to purpose and retention

commands.name: /secrets-scan
commands.does: Hunt credentials, report restricted, rotate on a live hit

commands.name: /findings
commands.does: The vulnerability ledger, restricted while unfixed

commands.name: /harden
commands.does: Remediation ordered by exploitability multiplied by impact

commands.name: /retest <id>
commands.does: Prove a fix by failing the original reproduction

commands.name: /clearance
commands.does: Issue the security clearance with conditions and untested surface

requires_human_approval_for: testing anything outside the written scope, or any third-party asset
any test against a production system or with real customer data
any test that could degrade availability, even briefly
issuing CLEARED WITH CONDITIONS, which needs a named owner per condition
disclosing a vulnerability outside the restricted channel, including to a vendor
accepting a known exploitable weakness into a release
